{{Short description|Data visualization method}}
[[File:Upset Plot.png|thumb|alt=An UpSet plot showing sets in the rows and intersections in the columns. The set sizes and intersection sizes are shown as bar charts.|An UpSet Plot showing how movie genres intersect. The largest intersection of two sets is the Comedy-Drama intersection. ]]
'''UpSet plots''' are a [[Data_and_information_visualization|data visualization]] method for showing set data with more than three intersecting [[Set (mathematics)|sets]]. 
UpSet shows intersections in a matrix, with the rows of the matrix corresponding to the sets, and the columns to the intersections between these sets (or vice versa). The size of the sets and of the intersections are shown as [[Bar chart|bar charts]]. 

== History ==

UpSet plots were first proposed in 2014.<ref name="upset_infovis_2014">{{cite journal |last1=Lex |first1=Alexander |last2=Gehlenborg |first2=Nils |last3=Strobelt |first3=Hendrik |last4=Vuillemot |first4=Romain |last5=Pfister |first5=Hanspeter |title=UpSet: Visualization of Intersecting Sets |journal=IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics |date=31 December 2014 |volume=20 |issue=12 |pages=1983–1992 |doi=10.1109/TVCG.2014.2346248|pmid=26356912 |pmc=4720993 }}</ref> The first prototype was implemented as an interactive, web-based application.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Lex |first1=Alexander |last2=Gehlenborg |first2=Nils |last3=Strobelt |first3=Hendrik |last4=Vuillemot |first4=Romain |last5=Pfister |first5=Hanspeter |url=http://vcg.github.io/upset/ | title="UpSet - Visualizing Intersecting Sets"}}</ref> UpSet plots are related to [[Mosaic plot|mosaic plots]], although mosaic plots are designed for categorical instead of set data. 

UpSet plots became popular as they became available as an [[R (programming language)|R]]-library based on [[ggplot2]],<ref name="upsetr">{{cite journal |last1=Conway |first1=Jake R |last2=Lex |first2=Alexander |last3=Gehlenborg |first3=Nils |title=UpSetR: an R package for the visualization of intersecting sets and their properties |journal=Bioinformatics |date=15 September 2017 |volume=33 |issue=18 |pages=2938–2940 |doi=10.1093/bioinformatics/btx364|pmid=28645171 |pmc=5870712 }}</ref> and were subsequently re-implemented in various programming languages, such as [[Python (programming language)|Python]], and others.<ref name="upset.app">{{cite web |last1=Lex |first1=Alexander |title=UpSet |url=https://upset.app/ |website=upset.app |access-date=18 February 2022 |language=en}}</ref> As of January 2024, UpSetR has been downloaded from [[CRAN (R programming language)|CRAN]] more than 1.5 million times, although it was last updated {{Time ago|2019-05-09}}.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Conway |first1=Jake R |last2=Gehlenborg |first2=Nils  |title=UpSetR |website=[[GitHub]] |date=9 May 2019 |url=https://github.com/hms-dbmi/UpSetR |access-date=23 August 2024}}</ref> UpSet plots are now frequently used instead of [[Venn diagram]]s, especially in life sciences.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Gadhave |first1=Kiran |title="UpSet 2: From Prototype to Tool" |url=https://vdl.sci.utah.edu/publications/2019_infovis_upset/ |access-date=28 April 2022}}</ref>

== Usage ==

[[File:UpSet Intersection Concept.svg|thumb|alt=An upset matrix is shown on the left, where each row corresponds to an intersection of multiple sets, which are shown in the columns. Three intersections (just in B; in A and B, but not in C; and in all of A, B, and C) are highlighted and the corresponding segments are shown in a Venn diagram. |Illustration showing how the rows of an UpSet plot correspond to the segments of a Venn diagram. ]]

[[File:UpSet Plot and a Corresponding Venn Diagram.svg|thumb|alt=An UpSet plot showing three sets (A, B, and C) and the corresponding Venn diagram. The size of the intersections (the cardinality) in the UpSet plot are visualized using labelled bar charts. The venn diagram labels the intersections. |An UpSet plot showing three sets, and the corresponding venn diagram.]]

UpSet plots visualize intersections between sets in a matrix. In a vertical UpSet plot, the columns of the matrix correspond to the sets, the rows correspond to the intersections. For each row, the cells that are part of an intersection are filled in. If there are multiple filled-in cells, they are connected with a line, to emphasize the reading direction of the plot. As sets vary in size, the size of the set is plotted as bar charts on top of the columns. The size of the intersections are shown aligned with the rows, also as bar charts. This layout facilitates the comparison between the sizes of individual intersections, as the size of the bars is easy to compare. UpSets can be used horizontally and vertically. 

UpSet plots can be sorted in various ways. A common sorting approach, for example, is to sort by cardinality (the size of an intersection), which places the biggest intersections on top. Alternative sortings are by the degree of the intersection, or by sets. 

UpSet plots can also be used to visualize attributes about the intersections by placing attribute visualizations next to the bar charts.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Gu |first1=Zuguang |title=UpSet plot |url=https://jokergoo.github.io/ComplexHeatmap-reference/book/upset-plot.html#example-with-the-genomic-regions }}</ref> Common choices for these attribute visualizations are compact visualization approaches for distributions, such as [[Box plot|box plots]], or [[violin plot|violin plots]].

Advanced features of UpSet plots include querying, grouping and aggregating data.<ref name="upset_infovis_2014"></ref> These features tend to be available only in interactive, web-based implementations of UpSet.<ref name="upset.app"></ref>

== Benefits and limitations == 

UpSet plots tend to perform better than Venn diagrams for larger numbers of sets and when it is desirable to also show contextual information about the set intersections.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Laura |first1=Ellis |title=Set Analysis: A face off between Venn diagrams and UpSet plots |url=https://www.littlemissdata.com/blog/set-analysis |website=Little Miss Data |access-date=28 April 2022}}</ref> For visualizing diagrams with less than three sets, or when there are only few intersections, Venn and [[Euler diagram]]s are generally preferred, because they tend to be more familiar and intuitive to read.<ref name="sets_2014_nature_methods">{{cite journal |last1=Lex |first1=Alexander |last2=Gehlenborg |first2=Nils |title=Sets and intersections |journal=Nature Methods |date=1 August 2014 |volume=11 |issue=8 |pages=779 |doi=10.1038/nmeth.3033|s2cid=39124565 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

UpSet plots are limited to displaying 20-30 sets, though specifics depends on the actual data.<ref name="sets_2014_nature_methods"></ref> An alternative approach for larger datasets is to show a [[co-occurrence heat map]], though these cannot show higher-order intersections<ref name="sets_2014_nature_methods"></ref>
